rationale: The acquired producer/test and exact-context consumer establish a local identity duty. Submit one fixed clean-copy check with real Peer-produced confirmations and independent destination correlation.

candidate.rationale: Fix the local correlation responsibility without turning permitted timeout into a liveness violation.

question.question: When one quorum heartbeat confirmation releases multiple pending ReadIndex requests from remote replicas, does the leader preserve each released request SystemCtx in the response sent to its origin?
question.importance: Losing correlation can discard already-qualified read readiness and strand an admitted batch until its timeout; no incorrect read value or deadline violation is asserted.
contexts: Distinct nonzero contexts for overlapping remote batches
event_paths: Peer.ReadIndex -> follower forwarding -> leader addRequest -> heartbeat response -> confirm prefix -> per-origin response -> follower ReadyToRead

supporting_behavior_ids.B-authority: Establishes stable current-term authority and resets pending read state on transition.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-replicate: Establishes current-term committed prefix required for read admission.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-readclient: Exact SystemCtx lookup provides the consumer duty and consequence of context substitution.
supporting_behavior_ids.B-persist: Defines normal update/save/send sequencing for a legal driver.

counterevidence: Local completions use each released record context; single-voter observer replies also preserve the request context.
Confirm intentionally raises released indices to the later confirmed index, so index equality alone cannot establish identity preservation.
A timeout is a permitted API outcome; the proposed question is the local response correlation duty rather than unconditional read success.
unknowns: Construct and observe a legal Peer/update history with overlapping remote contexts and confirmation of the later context, preserving caller and transport duties.
question.trigger_rationale: Tracker test expects released records to retain distinct contexts; remote response construction instead copies the single confirming heartbeat context. Exact-context client lookup supplies a concrete discriminator. A controlled Peer test is smaller than a NodeHost deployment and can observe actual emitted response identity without relying on timeouts.

obligation.description: When a current multi-voter leader releases a pending remote ReadIndex request after quorum confirmation and emits its ReadIndexResp to the requesting replica, the response must carry that released request’s SystemCtx unchanged, including when one confirmation releases several queued requests. The returned index may be advanced to the later confirmed safe index.

scope.description: Local correlation of an actually released remote read request to its emitted ReadIndexResp in a stable leader term and membership.
assumptions: Crash-fault operation with unmodified messages produced by configured peers.
Distinct nonzero SystemCtx values identify the pending requests; source identity and term are preserved through delivery.
excluded: Numeric completion deadlines or unconditional read availability
Wrong read values or linearizability violations
Restart and concurrent membership change during the confirmation

grounding.derivation: The tracker returns each qualified readStatus with its own context and origin (S-readtest explicitly expects distinct contexts for a released prefix). The follower exports exactly the reply context, and the client consumer matches only that context. Therefore a reply reporting qualification to a requesting replica must preserve that request context. Index promotion to a later safe index is allowed; substituting identity is not equivalent to that promotion.
grounding.applicability: Multi-voter leader, current-term commitment, stable term/membership, distinct contexts admitted from remote members and actually removed by one quorum confirmation. This is a local response-correlation duty, not a promise that all network requests succeed before a deadline.
alternatives: Local completion already uses each record context; the single-voter branch is outside this queued-prefix check.
Packet loss or client timeout alone would not violate this requirement.

associations.rationale: The per-origin response builder is the concrete consumer of each qualified request and its correlation identity.

bindings.description: Consumes confirmed readStatus records and emits per-origin ReadIndexResp or local ReadyToRead.
